items.summary: In his GrowSF questionnaire, Bastiany proposes launching MACPI, with licensed, unarmed martial artists and U.S. veterans as de-escalators in high-need areas, schools and transit corridors, piloted in Bayview with $2M from Prop A safety funds; his 100-day target is 25 MACPI patrols operating across District 10.
items.title: Martial Artists Community Protection Initiative (MACPI) pilot

citations.quote: Launch the Martial Artists Community Protection Initiative (MACPI), deploying licensed, unarmed Taekwondo/Karate black belts, martial artists, and US Veterans as de-escalators in high-need areas, schools, and transit corridors.
Pilot in Bayview hotspots with $2M from Prop A safety funds, measuring success via crime incident reductions.
Day 100 Metric: 25 MACPI patrols operational across D10; contracts signed with 10 businesses/schools; zero incidents on patrol routes.

items.summary: Bastiany's GrowSF questionnaire says he seeks federal Maritime Prosperity Zone designation to reactivate the shipyard with phytoremediation and clean manufacturing, and advocates that the Secretary of the Navy cancel the 26-year-old Lennar/5Point housing plan there; his 100-day target is a Board of Supervisors resolution introduced and a letter sent to the Secretary of the Navy.
items.title: Maritime Prosperity Zone designation for Hunters Point Naval Shipyard

citations.quote: Secure federal Maritime Prosperity Zone designation to reactivate shipyard with phytoremediation and clean manufacturing.
Day 100 Metric: BOS resolution introduced + letter to Secretary of Navy sent; MPZ pre-application filed with MARAD; first phytoremediation test plot active at shipyard.
I am now advocating that the Secretary of the Navy cancel the 26-year-old Lennar/5Point housing plan at Hunters Point

items.summary: Bastiany's GrowSF questionnaire proposes 10 barge-mounted prefab housing clusters (840 units, about 1,460 residents) in India Basin and Islais Creek at $1,000 to $2,500 a month, with rent-to-own options.
items.title: Maritime Atlantis for Housing barge villages

citations.quote: Roll out Maritime Atlantis for Housing Villages: 10 barge-mounted prefab clusters (840 units, ~1,460 residents) in India Basin/Islais Creek using Homes4Homeless space capsules at $1,000-$2,500/month (rent-to-own options building $42M resident equity).

items.summary: Bastiany's GrowSF questionnaire proposes a three-part transit plan: historic trolley shuttles from Evans to Sunnydale during the Islais Creek Bridge closure, a T-line extension along Geneva Avenue to Balboa Park BART, and a shoreline light rail line from Evans via India Basin, Candlestick and Bayshore.
items.title: D10 Connectivity Plan: trolley shuttles, T-line extension, shoreline rail

citations.quote: Implement the "D10 Connectivity Plan": (1) Historic trolley shuttles from Evans to Sunnydale during Islais Creek Bridge closure (2026-2028); (2) T-line extension along Geneva Avenue to Balboa Park BART for seamless SamTrans/Caltrain access; (3) Shoreline light rail from Evans via India Basin, Candlestick, and Bayshore with off-peak light freight to divert Prologis warehouse trucks
